title: GPU Specification
description: Schema for GPU Agent GPU specification data

name.description: Unique identifier slug for the GPU

category.description: GPU market segment: gaming (consumer graphics cards), workstation (professional visualization), or datacenter (enterprise/AI compute)

msrpUSD.description: Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Price in USD at launch. SOURCING REQUIREMENTS: Must be sourced from (1) the manufacturer's official website domain (nvidia.com, amd.com, intel.com), OR (2) verified by 3 independent credible sources, OR (3) for enterprise GPUs without official MSRP, an 'estimated MSRP' based on market pricing within 90 days of launch from 3+ sources (Wikipedia, tech news, reseller pricing at launch). All MSRP sources MUST be included in the references array. A note explaining the MSRP source MUST be added to the notes array. For estimated MSRPs, prefix note with 'Estimated MSRP of $XXX USD...' and explain the basis. For enterprise GPUs, note that pricing may vary by form factor (PCIe vs SXM) and memory size. Use null ONLY when no pricing data is available even from launch-time sources. For NVIDIA consumer cards, use Founder's Edition pricing.

tensorCoreCount.description: Number of matrix units: NVIDIA Tensor Cores, AMD AI Accelerators (RDNA 3 and later) or Matrix Cores (CDNA), Intel XMX engines. Null or omitted where the part has no matrix unit (NVIDIA Pascal and older, GTX 16-series, AMD RDNA 2 and GCN).

fp32TFLOPS.description: FP32-class throughput a training or inference workload gets, in TFLOPS. Where the part has a hardware TF32 matrix path, this is TF32 Tensor Core (NVIDIA Ampere and later) or TF32 Matrix (AMD CDNA 3) throughput without sparsity. Otherwise it is FP32 vector throughput (CUDA cores, stream processors, Xe vector engines), as on NVIDIA Volta and older, AMD RDNA and GCN, Intel Xe2, and AMD CDNA 4, whose TF32 is software-emulated. NVIDIA GeForce runs dense TF32 at the FP32 vector rate; professional and datacenter Ampere, Ada and Blackwell run it at 2x, except the L40, which runs it at 1x (90.5 TF32 and 90.5 FP32 vector per its datasheet); A100/A30 and Hopper run it at 7x to 8x. Where a professional part publishes no dense TF32 figure, derive it as the published sparse FP16, FP8 or FP4 Tensor figure divided by 4 (Ampere), 8 (Ada) or 16 (Blackwell), and say so in the notes. Never the sparse TF32 figure. The notes must give the other figure (FP32 vector, or TF32 dense) and its source; scripts/validate-specs.ts checks the other metrics' ratios to this one per architecture.

fp16TFLOPS.description: FP16 throughput on the highest-rate path the hardware has, in TFLOPS. NVIDIA Volta and later: FP16 Tensor Core with 2:4 structured sparsity, as NVIDIA publishes it (for GeForce, the FP16-accumulate figure; for consumer Blackwell, which publishes only AI TOPS, AI TOPS / 4); Volta and Turing have no sparsity, so their dense figure. NVIDIA Pascal and older: FP16 vector (P100 is 2x FP32). AMD RDNA 3 and RDNA 4: FP16 Matrix (WMMA) without sparsity, as AMD publishes it, never the FP16 Vector figure. AMD RDNA 2 and GCN: packed FP16 vector (2x FP32 where Rapid Packed Math exists, otherwise 1x). Intel Arc: FP16 XMX as Intel publishes it. NVIDIA sparse versus AMD RDNA dense is a deliberate asymmetry (2026-06-03): each vendor's headline figure is kept, and RDNA 3 has no hardware sparsity. Use int8TOPS for a like-for-like comparison.

int8TOPS.description: INT8 throughput on the highest-rate path the hardware has (Tensor Core, Matrix Core, WMMA, XMX; the DP4A ALU instruction on Volta), without sparsity, in TOPS, for every vendor. NVIDIA Ampere and later publish the 2:4 sparse figure as the headline; store half of it. NVIDIA Volta and Turing, AMD and Intel publish dense figures. Null if the part has no INT8 rate.

fp8TFLOPS.description: FP8 matrix/tensor throughput without sparsity, in TFLOPS, for every vendor (no NVIDIA/AMD asymmetry here). Where only the sparse figure is published, store half of it. Null where the hardware has no FP8 matrix path (NVIDIA Ampere and older, AMD RDNA 3 and older, Intel Xe2), or where no source was found, in which case list it in unverifiedSpecs.

fp4TFLOPS.description: FP4 matrix/tensor throughput without sparsity, in TFLOPS, for every vendor. NVIDIA consumer Blackwell publishes only sparse AI TOPS; store AI TOPS / 2. AMD CDNA 4 publishes a single MXFP4 rate, stored as dense. Null where the hardware has no FP4 path (everything before NVIDIA Blackwell and AMD CDNA 4), or where no source was found, in which case list it in unverifiedSpecs.

memoryBandwidthGBs.description: Peak memory bandwidth in GB/s (decimal gigabytes per second) as the manufacturer publishes it for the card's VRAM. Excludes cache bandwidth and AMD's Infinity Cache 'effective bandwidth'. For multi-die parts, the total for the package.

maxTDPWatts.description: Maximum board power in watts as the manufacturer publishes it: NVIDIA's Total Graphics Power or Max Power Consumption, AMD's Total Board Power, Intel's Total Board Power. For a configurable part, the highest configuration the manufacturer lists.

gpuArchitecture.description: GPU architecture name (e.g., Ampere, RDNA 3, Blackwell)

supportedHardwareOperations.description: List of supported hardware operations (e.g., FP16, INT8, TF32)

supportedCUDAComputeCapability.description: CUDA compute capability version for NVIDIA GPUs

lastModified.description: Last modified timestamp in ISO 8601 format

summary.description: Detailed summary of the GPU specifications and features

references.description: URLs to reference documentation and specs

notes.description: Additional notes about the specifications and how they were calculated

unverifiedSpecs.description: Field names that could not be confirmed from authoritative sources and were deliberately left null rather than guessed. Distinguishes 'hardware genuinely lacks this' from 'we couldn't find the data'. Each entry requires a matching notes entry starting 'NOT FOUND: <field>' explaining what was searched.

manufacturerIdentifiers.description: Official identifiers from the GPU manufacturer (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel). Only include model numbers, part numbers, and SKUs - NOT PCI device IDs or other hardware bus identifiers. Manufacturers often have MULTIPLE identifier types - for example, NVIDIA uses both 'Product SKU' (e.g., PG133 SKU 242) AND 'NVPN' part numbers (e.g., 900-2G133-0080-000). Include ALL official identifiers found in datasheets and product documentation.

type.description: The type of identifier. Common types by manufacturer: NVIDIA: 'product_sku' (e.g., 'PG133 SKU 242'), 'nvpn' (e.g., '900-2G133-0080-000'), 'board_id' (e.g., 'PG133'). AMD: 'opn' (Ordering Part Number), 'model_number'. Intel: 'product_code', 'mm_number' (Material Master), 'spec_code'. DO NOT include PCI device IDs, vendor IDs, or other hardware bus identifiers.

value.description: The identifier value exactly as shown in official documentation

thirdPartyProducts.description: Products from third-party companies (OEMs, AIB partners) based on this GPU. These are companies that manufacture graphics cards using the GPU chip. For datacenter GPUs: Dell, HP/HPE, Lenovo, Supermicro, PNY. For consumer GPUs: ASUS, MSI, Gigabyte, EVGA, Sapphire, PowerColor, XFX, Zotac, PNY. A single company may have MULTIPLE products with different identifiers - include them as separate entries.

company.description: Company name. Use consistent names: 'Dell' (not 'Dell Technologies'), 'HP' or 'HPE', 'ASUS' (not 'Asus'), 'MSI', 'Gigabyte', 'PNY', 'EVGA', 'Sapphire', 'PowerColor', 'XFX', 'Zotac', 'Supermicro', 'Lenovo'

productName.description: The company's official product name for this card (e.g., 'NVIDIA L40S 48GB GDDR6 350W PCIe x16 DW FHFL GPU' for Dell, 'ROG STRIX GeForce RTX 4090 OC Edition' for ASUS)

identifier.description: The identifier value (part number, SKU, or model number). IMPORTANT: This must be a unique identifier, NOT the product name. If identifier equals productName, the entry is invalid and should be removed.

identifierType.description: Type of identifier: 'part_number' = Internal inventory/ordering code, often alphanumeric (e.g., Dell '7WK28', HP 'L57056-001', Supermicro 'GPU-NRTXA6000-AC'). 'sku' = Stock Keeping Unit, retail/sales identifier (e.g., PNY 'TCSL40SPCIE-PB'). 'model_number' = Consumer-facing product identifier (e.g., ASUS 'ROG-STRIX-RTX4090-O24G-GAMING').
